title: Dissipation-induced Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev physics in many-body cavity quantum electrodynamics
authors: Pietro Pacchioni, Filippo Ferrari, Vincenzo Savona, Matteo Seclì
abstract: We show that cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) devices can realize dissipative Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) physics, a paradigmatic setting for quantum chaos in open many-body systems. Ultracold fermions with disordered, all-to-all cavity-mediated interactions provide two complementary routes: atomic spontaneous emission in a single-mode cavity and photon leakage from a multimode cavity. Strikingly, both converge to the same non-Hermitian random-matrix universality despite originating from integrable and chaotic closed-system limits, respectively. In the single-mode case, dissipation therefore creates quantum chaos from an integrable Hamiltonian. We trace this convergence to a tunable growth in dissipative rank, controlled, respectively, by the Lamb-Dicke parameter and the cavity-mode spacing. The resulting chaos leaves a dynamical fingerprint: a crossover from long-lived prethermal memory to rapid thermalization, visible in single-atom-resolved densities.
summary: This paper demonstrates that cavity QED devices can realize dissipative Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev physics, a key model for quantum chaos. By analyzing both single-mode spontaneous emission and multi-mode cavity leakage, the authors show that dissipation drives the system into a universal non-Hermitian random matrix universality class. This offers a powerful experimental route to study the emergence of quantum chaos in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how dissipation can induce Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) physics, a model for quantum chaos, in open many-body systems.
main_result: Both single-mode and multi-mode cavity loss mechanisms successfully realize universal open SYK physics, demonstrating that dissipation can generate quantum chaos even when starting from integrable Hamiltonians.
method: The analysis relies on calculating spectral form factors (SFFs) and singular spectral form factors ($\sigma$SFFs) derived from the Liouvillian master equation to diagnose the transition to quantum chaos.
model_or_system: The system is based on Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics (cQED) using ultracold fermionic atoms interacting with a cavity. The dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating cavity losses and atomic spontaneous emission.
key_observables: Dissipative Spectral Form Factors (DSFF), Singular Spectral Form Factors ($\sigma$SFF), and the crossover dynamics observed in single-atom-resolved densities ($n_j(t)$).
important_parameters: Lamb-Dicke parameter ($\eta$) for spontaneous emission, and the cavity-mode spacing parameter ($\delta	ilde{\omega}$) for multi-mode loss.
main_assumptions: The analysis often requires unfolding the spectrum to compare results with universal Random Matrix Theory (RMT) predictions, and approximations like adiabatic elimination are used in the multi-mode case.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $\sigma$SFF and DSFF for both single-mode and multi-mode loss routes, showing convergence to RMT predictions, alongside plots of atomic density relaxation ($n_j(t)$) demonstrating the prethermal-to-thermalization crossover.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the effective Hamiltonian and the master equation for both single-mode and multi-mode cQED. It then applies advanced RMT diagnostics ($\sigma$SFF, DSFF) to show the universal emergence of SYK physics, linking the control parameters ($\eta, \delta	ilde{\omega}$) to the degree of induced chaos.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable platform (cQED) to study fundamental concepts of quantum chaos and thermalization in open systems, bridging theoretical models like SYK with experimental quantum optics setups.
